name: runbook
title: Runbook
summary: Works an alert against the written runbook and takes the first remediation step only once a person has said yes — with every node and call recorded.
blurb: The 2am agent, with the governance bolted on at the seams rather than written into it. It reads the runbook before it reads the metrics, because a runbook's steps include what not to do and that is the expensive part to rediscover at 2am; it checks the upstreams before it touches the service that is complaining; and it treats a failure within half an hour of a deploy as that deploy until proved otherwise. Then it stops. The two tools that change production are gated by a middleware the operator installs, so a call to restart or scale suspends the whole run into its session and waits — the process can exit, and the yes can arrive from another terminal, another machine, or an hour later from somebody's phone. A second middleware records every node and every call as events, and an encoder turns the run into one JSON object per line, so an incident leaves a file. Nothing in the flow names any of the three: the author chose what the agent can reach, and whoever runs it chooses what it may do unsupervised and what gets written down. Handing this bundle to a stricter team means handing them the same bundle with different flags.
